description:
Project: On-prem offline artifact signing (Redwood Private – VPC + on-prem packaging).

Goal
- Enable customers with air-gapped environments to install/upgrade Redwood Private using offline bundles that are cryptographically signed by Redwood and verified during install.
- Reduce supply-chain risk by ensuring integrity and provenance of: installer binaries, Helm charts/manifests, container image references, model/runtime artifacts, and any required dependency packages.

Scope
- Define an offline bundle format (bundle layout + manifest) and a deterministic build process.
- Implement bundle signing in the release pipeline (CI/CD) with protected keys and auditable steps.
- Implement verification in the on-prem installer (and/or preflight tooling) that blocks install on signature/manifest mismatch, with clearly documented break-glass paths.
- Add audit/telemetry hooks appropriate for private deployments (what gets logged locally; what can be exported).
- Update public/private deployment docs and support runbooks.

Out of scope (initial phase)
- Full multi-party customer key delegation for signing (customer-signed bundles) beyond a documented future plan.
- Overhauling the entire private deployment packaging system; this project piggybacks on existing bundle/installer architecture.

Key stakeholders
- Product (Private): Vivek Kulkarni (requirements, rollout, GA criteria)
- Release Engineering: Connor O'Brien (release train integration, key ceremony, reproducibility)
- Build/CI: Sahana Iyer (pipeline hardening, CI checks, artifact integrity gates)
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei (threat model, key management, auditing)
- Security leadership / GRC: Dr. Aisha Rahman, Olga Petrov (policy alignment, evidence, customer security reviews)
- Infra/SRE: Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher (operational readiness, incident playbooks)
- Solutions Engineering / PS: Fatima Noor, Colin O'Donnell, Bruno Silva (customer requirements, pilots)

Timeline (example, realistic)
- Phase 0 (2–3 weeks): customer requirements + format proposal + threat model + ADR
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): implement bundle manifest + signing pipeline + installer verification + docs drafts
- Phase 2 (3–4 weeks): pilot with 2–3 air-gapped customers, harden error messages/runbooks, key rotation procedure
- Phase 3 (GA): ship in a Redwood Private release, add support playbooks and compliance evidence mapping

Deliverables
- Confluence: PRD, design doc, ADR, threat model, standards/policy pages, runbooks, customer-facing guide, release notes
- GitHub: PRs across redwood-private-installer, redwood-helm-charts, redwood, redwood-docs, security tooling
- Linear: initiative tracking + execution tickets, dependencies, rollout checklist
- Slack: coordination threads across release/security/infra/support
- Drive: working drafts, checklists, pilot notes, validation matrices
- Customer-facing artifacts: sales/SE calls (Fireflies), CRM notes (HubSpot), security/procurement email threads (Gmail)
- Support readiness: Jira tickets for pilot feedback and early issues
